Mateo / team — thanks for the flag. Draft language below (Option 1 = tranche split; Option 2 = blended). I'm also attaching a one-page redline you can drop into the SOW.

Option 1 (Tranche split - preferred):
"Billing Calculation: Usage within each billing period will be allocated to the defined pricing bands sequentially. Units falling within Band A will be billed at Band A rates, units within Band B will be billed at Band B rates, and so forth. Example: for 120,000 units where Band A = 0–100,000 at $0.015/unit and Band B = 100,001–250,000 at $0.012/unit, the invoice will charge (100,000 x $0.015) + (20,000 x $0.012) = $1,560.

Option 2 (Blended interpolation):
"Billing Calculation: For any billing period where total usage falls between defined bands, the per-unit rate will be calculated by linear interpolation between the adjacent band rates and applied to the total usage. Example: using the same band rates and 120,000 units, blended rate = $0.015 - ((120,000-100,000)/(250,000-100,000)) * ($0.015-$0.012) = $0.0146; charge = 120,000 x $0.0146 = $1,752.

Minimums / True-up:
"Minimum Commitment: Customer agrees to the Minimum Monthly Commitment set forth in the Order Form. If actual usage in any billing period is less than the Minimum Monthly Commitment, Customer will be invoiced for the Minimum Monthly Commitment amount for that period (i.e., a true-up to the Minimum), unless the parties agree otherwise in writing. The true-up is not an additional surcharge beyond the stated Minimum Monthly Commitment.

Notes: 1) Tranche split preserves marginal pricing discipline and is easier for billing systems; 2) Blended interpolation materially changes unit economics at band edges (see examples). Recommend Option 1 unless Lumina requires blended billing.

Attachment: proposed_pricing_guardrail_clause.docx
